evidence.requirements: All functional points are met. The start page shows title, date/time, 'EUR n per guest' and '<n> seats left' (TastingList.tsx:28-34, start.jpg). There is a 'Book <title>' link for each tasting (TastingList.tsx:45-47). The form has the labels Name/Email/Guests, a 1-8 limit and a 'Book' button (BookingForm.tsx:80-156). Seat limits are enforced on the server (store.ts:55) and errors are shown next to their field (form.jpg). The confirmation has the heading 'Booking confirmed' plus tasting, guests, total and reference (Confirmation.tsx:24-38, confirmation.jpg). /staff has a Password field and Sign in button, with the password read from STAFF_PASSWORD (index.ts:4). Bookings are grouped with name/email/guests/reference and a Cancel button that frees seats (StaffPage.tsx:110-155, store.ts:70-75, staff.jpg). There are clear fully-booked and phone layouts (.playwright-mcp/home-375-soldout2.png). The stack is React, Express, react-router, react-hook-form, zod and Tailwind. Partly met: the Process requirement (spec, plan, review phases) left no artifacts in the repo (no specs, ADRs or docs).
evidence.correctness: Booking does its check and insert in one synchronous step, so concurrent requests cannot overbook (store.ts:50-61), and tests cover this with 2 and 6 parallel requests (app.test.ts:211-230). Exact-remaining and one-over cases are handled with singular/plural messages (app.ts:26-29). Cancelling removes the booking, so seats are counted again; a second cancel of the same reference returns 404 (store.ts:70-75). Zod rejects non-integer, string, NaN, 0 and 9 guests and trims name/email (schemas.ts:5-13). Malformed JSON gets a 400, an oversized body a 413, and a bad URL encoding a 400 (app.ts:135-160). After a 409 the form reloads the tasting so the seat count is current (BookingForm.tsx:71). Minor: the confirmation lives only in router state, so a reload loses it, but the page handles that case (Confirmation.tsx:9-19).
evidence.security: React escapes all output and there is no dangerouslySetInnerHTML. The password is compared with timingSafeEqual over SHA-256 digests, so different lengths do not throw (auth.ts:21-27,56). Session tokens come from randomBytes(32) and expire after 8 hours on the server, and sign-out deletes them (auth.ts:37-45,71-84). The cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict, and Secure is set behind a trusted proxy (app.ts:31-33). After 5 failed sign-ins in 15 minutes a client IP is locked out for 15 minutes with Retry-After (auth.ts:61-67). Helmet is on, staff API responses are no-store, and the server refuses to start without STAFF_PASSWORD. TRUST_PROXY=true is rejected to prevent IP spoofing (index.ts:10-15). No secrets are in the code. Gap: public booking POSTs have no rate limit, so a script could fill all seats.
evidence.code_quality: The structure is small and clear: server/app, store and auth; shared schemas, tastings and format; client pages and api. The zod schemas are shared by client and server. Result types are discriminated unions (store.ts:9-12, auth.ts:10-13), and app.ts needs no try/catch because store and auth return results instead of throwing. Time is injectable for tests. Names are clear and functions small. Minor: the staff status line uses green 'success' styling even for the failure message (StaffPage.tsx:87,105).
evidence.tests: Supertest API tests cover listing, totals, all validation messages, the exact-capacity boundary, 409 messages, parallel overbooking, cookie flags, lockout, session expiry, cancel freeing seats, and 401s on staff routes (app.test.ts). There are unit tests for the store, auth (lockout windows, expiry), schema boundaries (100/101 characters, guests 0/1/8/9/2.5/NaN) and formatting. Client RTL tests cover start-page labels, the disabled fully-booked button, field errors with aria-invalid, server 409 mapping, confirmation content, sign-in, lockout and cancel. Entry-point tests check that a missing STAFF_PASSWORD or TRUST_PROXY=true makes startup fail (index.test.ts). There is no end-to-end browser test of the built app.
evidence.ux_design: The screenshots show a coherent winery look: deep wine header with a gold rule, serif headings, cream cards and pill buttons (start.jpg). Seat badges change colour, and fully booked tastings get a badge, a label and a disabled button (home-375-soldout2.png). The form puts a wine-coloured tasting summary beside it, with a clear inline red error (form.jpg). The confirmation card is clean and has guidance about the reference (confirmation.jpg). The staff page has clear tables per tasting with seat totals (staff.jpg). Weaknesses: there are no images or imagery, so it feels somewhat generic. Cancel has no confirmation step and is a plain text link, and the staff table needs horizontal scrolling on phones (min-w-[32rem]).
evidence.accessibility: The page uses lang=en, real labels tied to inputs, aria-invalid and aria-describedby pointing to error text with role=alert (BookingForm.tsx:83-143). react-hook-form moves focus to the first invalid field. There are a global :focus-visible gold outline (styles.css:22-25), nav/main/footer landmarks, table th scope=col, an sr-only actions header, a role=status for cancel results, and 44px minimum touch targets. Contrast problems: gold #a8844a dates on paper (TastingList.tsx:29) and the gold 'TASTING' label on wine (BookingForm.tsx:36) are about 3.3-3.7:1 for small text, below WCAG AA's 4.5:1. The disabled button text is low contrast.
evidence.simplicity: Runtime dependencies are limited to express, helmet, cookie-parser, react, react-router, react-hook-form, @hookform/resolvers and zod, which fit the brief's request to use established libraries. Source is about 700 lines. There is no needless abstraction; ui.ts is just shared class strings. The custom lockout and session map in auth.ts (86 lines) is reasonable but could have used existing middleware such as express-rate-limit.
evidence.maintainability: There is no README, so nothing documents STAFF_PASSWORD, TRUST_PROXY, PORT, the dev workflow (npm run dev plus dev:api) or staff usage. There is no CI configuration, no docs, ADRs or specs, and no changelog or release approach beyond version 0.1.0. Node is only 'engines >=22', with no .nvmrc; dependencies use caret ranges, but package-lock.json is present. The test, typecheck and lint scripts exist and the regression tests are strong, which helps a newcomer. The .playwright-mcp folder of agent screenshots was shipped in app/ (it is gitignored).

unmet_requirements: Process: no specification, plan, ADR or review artifacts in the repository despite the brief requiring a full spec-driven process
Look and feel: small-text contrast for gold dates and labels falls below WCAG AA (polish and accessibility partly met)
strengths: Correct, well-tested booking logic: an atomic seat check, a concurrency test, boundary and 409 messages, and cancel freeing seats
Strong staff security: timing-safe comparison, random server-side sessions with expiry and logout, hardened cookies, per-IP lockout, helmet, fail-fast on a missing STAFF_PASSWORD
Polished, coherent winery design with clear error, success and fully-booked states and a working phone layout; accessible form error wiring
issues: No README or docs: STAFF_PASSWORD, TRUST_PROXY, the dev workflow and staff usage are undocumented, and there are no ADRs or specs
No CI pipeline, no release/versioning approach and no pinned Node version (.nvmrc), so maintainability relies on someone discovering the npm scripts
Gold small text (dates, 'TASTING' label) fails WCAG AA contrast; Cancel has no confirmation step and its failure message is styled as success; no rate limit on public bookings
review.verdict: The app is functionally complete, correct under concurrency, secure, nicely designed and backed by a thorough test suite, so the code itself is ready for the winery. What holds it back is the missing README, CI, decision docs and runtime pinning, which would leave the next developer guessing about setup and configuration, plus a few contrast and staff-UX rough edges.
